newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says Canada gold find significant.
newsitem.headline: BHP says Canada gold find significant.

text.p: The Broken Hill Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Monday its gold find in the Hope Bay region in Canada's Northwest Territories was one of the most significant discoveries the company had ever made.
The head of BHP's minerals division, Dick Carter told a media and analysts briefing that BHP was focusing its efforts in the region at four gold prospects along a 70 km strike length.
"Boston is the most advanced of the prospects and a potentially mineable resource was established by underground evaluation last year," Carter said.
Asked how large the potential resource was, Carter said, "About two to three million ounces (of gold) is the likely resource from drilling so far, but that is not definitive."
Analysts said the remoteness of the Hope Bay greenstone belt meant any project development would require a substantial resource to be an economic proposition.

"In other areas of the Hope Bay belt, further surface drilling of the three prospects next targeted for evaluation is underway. It is hoped that this programme can bring more prospects to the bulk sample stage in 1998," Carter said.
Carter said although the project was promising any mining development in Canada needed to meet strict standards relating to environmental concerns.
BHP was unlikely to sole-develop any project in the region, preferring to find a joint venture partner to share the risk, Carter said.
